# Nominal interface default forwarding

An original Java body forwards one reference argument and reference result to a
default inherited through a direct interface. Only its bridge access bit is
encoded; every compiler Code byte, descriptor and other attribute stays intact.
The interface graph includes an unrelated branch and a redundant direct marker.

Frozen callers, reflection, method handles and a rebuilt caller check original
dispatch, nominal identities, raw input bits, virtual callbacks, reentry, partial
construction and exact checked/runtime/Error identity. All emitted Java compiles,
and all original entries and metadata are checked with the established bridge-bit
disclosure. Independent wrong programs qualify the observer before recovery.
